reading.body:
CyrusOne Lewisville DFW2 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity, placing it 12th among 19 Texas facilities with disclosed figures and just 2.5 percent of the state's 475 MW announced load.

At 40 kW per rack, 12 MW supports roughly 300 racks, a scale that is small for frontier AI training clusters. The facility's 200,000 square feet of technical space and its compliance certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 qualify it for regulated workloads, but those certifications do not signal AI-specific capability.

Texas has 133 mapped data center sites, yet most publish no capacity, so the 19 facilities with disclosed figures are only a partial view of the state's supply. The data does not include grid headroom or expansion plans, so it cannot show whether this campus can grow to meet AI demand.
